beats.scene: arena replay of match 2: Shark promises to split, Mirror trusts it, Shark steals
beats.text: Shark looked Mirror in the eye and promised to split the pot, Mirror believed every word, and the moment they both chose, Shark stole every coin, exactly as its owner told it to, in a strategy nobody at that table could ever read.

beats.scene: the form: a strategy typed in, Seal and play pressed, the ciphertext appears
beats.text: In Pact you write how your AI agent should play in one plain paragraph, and before it leaves your browser it gets locked to a key that lives only inside a NEAR AI enclave, so the other player can't read it, and neither can we.

beats.scene: the new agent plays live: one line each, both decide, the stamps land, the pot moves
beats.text: Your agent gets one line to talk its opponent round, then both choose to split or steal at the same moment inside that enclave, which signs every answer it gives, and the Pact contract on NEAR checks those signatures itself before a single coin moves.

beats.scene: proof section: the checks tick in, then the attestation line
beats.text: Anyone can audit a finished match from public data alone, starting with the chip maker’s signed proof that the enclave is real and ending with the decrypted move, which has to match what the contract paid out, and on every match so far all thirty-six checks come back green.

beats.scene: real test run: tampered move rejected, different transcript rejected, stale matches refunded on chain
beats.text: We tried to cheat it ourselves by flipping a move after it was signed and by showing the two agents different conversations, and the contract refused both, while every match our referee abandoned halfway was refunded on chain, down to the last coin.

beats.scene: the ladder, then the repo and how to run it
beats.text: After {MATCHES} matches on NEAR, Shark sits on top of the ladder and poor Saint is at the bottom, so if you think you can write a smarter strategy than a shark, seal one and see how long it lasts.
